rationale: The change correctly identifies and neutralizes the cause of the collapsed control. `MultiSelect` forwards the caller's `className` to both its outer wrapper (MultiSelect.tsx:352) and the inner PrimeReact root (MultiSelect.tsx:391), so the previous `flex-1` landed next to `h-[44px] py-[5px]` (MultiSelect.tsx:229). Inside a `flex flex-col` parent, `flex-1`'s `flex: 1 1 0%` resolves against the vertical axis and outranks the height declaration, collapsing the field. Dropping `flex-1` restores the 44px height, and the new row-flex wrapper gives `fullWidth`'s `flex-grow` a horizontal axis so the control still fills its container. Presentation-only: no props, state, data flow, or API surface changed. Gates verified on a clean `npm ci` install - typecheck exit 0, lint exit 0, unit 509 files / 5323 passed / 1 skipped, gitleaks `no leaks found`. One non-blocking nit recorded (CR-001).

findings.summary: `gap-2` on the new wrapper is inert - the div has exactly one child.
findings.detail: `<div className="flex gap-2">` wraps only `<MultiSelect />`. `gap` applies between flex items, so with a single item it never renders. `className="flex"` alone is sufficient and states the intent - supplying a row axis for `flex-grow` - without implying a sibling that does not exist.

follow_ups.summary: `MultiSelect` applies the caller's `className` to two elements in two different flex contexts (MultiSelect.tsx:352 outer wrapper, MultiSelect.tsx:391 inner PrimeReact root).
follow_ups.detail: Every layout class any consumer passes is silently applied twice. This is the underlying cause of EPMCDME-14073 and will keep producing similar defects. Out of scope here - MultiSelect is used app-wide and the change needs its own ticket with a full regression pass.
